description:
ASTROSINT — LOOKING BEYOND EARTH

What if OSINT didn't stop at Earth?

We’re building a team for NASA Space Apps, combining OSINT, AI, data, mapping and space science.

No perfect CV. Just curiosity, critical thinking and the courage to look where others don't.

Observe. Analyze. Connect. Discover.

summary:
AstrOsint01 is an accessible, interactive research prototype developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge “Be An Earth System Trend Detective!”

The project explores changes in terrestrial water storage (TWSa) and model-derived groundwater storage residuals (GWSa) across two study areas: California's Central Valley and the Taoudeni–Tanezrouft Basin.

Through the Water Signal Explorer, users can select regions, compare water variables and time periods, and investigate environmental trends. Evidence Delta compares trends across different time windows, while Evidence Constellation makes the evidence chain, data provenance, limitations, and verification needs visible.

Inspired by NASA GRACE/GRACE-FO satellite observations and GLDAS modelling concepts, the current prototype uses embedded representative monthly series rather than a live NASA data feed.
Accessibility is a core design principle. We specifically considered people with photosensitive epilepsy by avoiding flashing, strobing and rapid visual effects. The Explorer includes reduced-motion support, a dedicated Safe Mode, keyboard navigation, readable data tables and clear text explanations. These safeguards aim to make scientific exploration more inclusive, although they do not replace clinical safety certification.
Our goal is to make Earth observation understandable, accessible and evidence-driven.
details: AstrOsint01 – An Accessible Earth Observation Explorer AstrOsint01 is an interactive research prototype designed to help people explore and understand changes in terrestrial water storage. It focuses on two study areas: California's Central Valley and the Taoudeni–Tanezrouft Basin. The Water Signal Explorer allows users to select a region, compare Total Water Storage Anomalies (TWSa) and model-derived Groundwater Storage Anomalies (GWSa), and investigate trends across different time periods. Evidence Delta compares changes across time windows, while Evidence Constellation makes the evidence chain, data provenance, limitations and verification needs visible. The project draws on scientific concepts associated with NASA's GRACE and GRACE-FO satellite observations and GLDAS land-surface modelling. The current prototype uses embedded representative monthly datasets rather than a live NASA data connection. Trends are descriptive and are not presented as forecasts or proof of causation. We developed a browser-based interactive experience using HTML, CSS and JavaScript, hosted through GitHub Pages. No specialised hardware or software installation is required. Our creative approach combines Earth observation, OSINT-inspired evidence verification, geospatial exploration and accessible data storytelling. Instead of simply displaying charts, the project guides users through a process of detecting, comparing, verifying and exploring environmental signals. Accessibility was a core design consideration, particularly for people with photosensitive epilepsy. We avoided flashing, strobing and rapid visual effects and included reduced-motion support, Safe Mode, keyboard navigation, readable data tables and text explanations. The expected impact is to make complex Earth science more understandable, transparent and inclusive, encouraging critical thinking about water resources and environmental change.​
